text:
emma: Quick question — thinking about regional control-plane visibility: should we push per-customer private endpoints into their VPCs, or stick with a global CP and use ephemeral peering/tunnels for most tenants? tradeoffs on routing, IP preservation, and ops overhead?

raj: tl;dr: per-customer endpoints = simpler traffic path & IP preservation, but increases resource count (ENIs/peering attachments) and ops/config surface. ephemeral peers reduce idle cost but add setup complexity.

liam: +1. Also per-customer endpoints make allowlist/egress fingerprints way easier for customers (they see stable source IPs). important for enterprise customers.

morgan: FYI our cost sim from last month: maintaining thousands of idle private endpoints drove NAT/ENI costs higher than expected during low-util periods. ephemeral peers looked cheaper in compute alone.

charlie: ephemeral peering sounds attractive but watch for route table churn + AWS attachment quotas. If we create/destroy attachments per onboarding event we might hit limits or throttle.

emma: good point. what about using a central TGW/transit model vs per-VPC peering? TGW reduces number of attachments but centralizes a failure domain.

raj: TGW tradeoffs: fewer route entries but introduces a bottleneck (and cross-account attachments complexity). Also TGW may not preserve source ip semantics for some flows, need to verify.

liam: note on IP preservation: for some customers we must preserve source IP for their downstream allowlists. If TGW or a relay NATs us, that breaks their security posture.

morgan: proposed hybrid: reserve per-customer private endpoints for high-SLA / compliance customers, use ephemeral peering or shared relay for self-serve tenants. can gate by plan.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary: ephemeral-peering-broker v0.1 deployed to staging — logs: https://staging.redwood/peering-canary :rocket:

charlie: auth model question: how do agents authenticate over ephemeral links? mTLS with short-lived certs? JWT over an encrypted channel?

emma: leaning mTLS + short cert TTL. we already have a CA flow for agents, so minting client certs per ephemeral session seems consistent. but adds rotation logic.

raj: also need observable breadcrumbs: map which CP node served which tenant (for audits and debugging). Tag peering resources and emit telemetry events during handshake.

liam: additional ops: route propagation and limit impact. quick check: AWS route limit per VPC is finite; if we scale to many tenants we need TGW or aggregation.

morgan: other gotcha: cross-account peering may require acceptance flows and additional IAM steps. ephemeral broker can handle acceptance but complicates onboarding UX.

charlie: prototype idea for broker: tenant agent calls control-plane broker with signed intent, broker provisions peering attachment, mints short cert, then agent establishes mTLS over the new path. broker tears down after idle TTL.

emma: sounds reasonable. can we guarantee reasonable cold-start latency for control-plane calls? heartbeats vs on-demand?

liam: for control-plane heartbeats we may want persistent lightweight sessions (keepalive) for critical tenants; ephemeral for low-traffic ones. fallback to global API over public egress if peering setup fails.

morgan: cost/ops checklist: (1) route quotas + TGW pricing (2) NAT/ENI cost for per-customer endpoints (3) broker infra + state (4) cert minting/rotation overhead.

raj: I'll build a route-quota matrix and run scale sims. charlie can spin up the broker spike. liam will validate TGW path semantics (IP preservation/MTU) and limits.

charlie: I'll prototype the broker flow in staging and include acceptance/failover cases. will add simple metrics for setup latency + success rate.

emma: assign: raj + charlie + liam. ETA: rough findings by Fri. If we converge on hybrid, we should draft an interface contract: authentication handshake, tagging requirements, and fallback semantics.

liam: small note — check AWS PrivateLink vs peering for cross-account connectivity; PrivateLink preserves some semantics and avoids route table churn but has different pricing and scalability tradeoffs.

morgan: +1 on PrivateLink eval. It might give better isolation for enterprise tenants.

emma: thanks all. please drop short comments here if you hit blockers. otherwise we'll sync on Fri slot. :thumbsup:
